title: UV Light Revealed Camouflage on a 125-Million-Year-Old Crocodile
mediaSource: Montsecosuchus depereti fossil UV camouflage crocodile Spain

scenes.title: A 125-million-year-old crocodile still had a pattern
scenes.narration: When scientists examined an ancient crocodile relative from Spain under ultraviolet light, striped patterns appeared on its tail.

scenes.title: UV revealed details hidden in normal light
scenes.narration: Skin and soft-tissue traces that were difficult to see under ordinary light became much clearer under ultraviolet illumination.

scenes.title: The tail showed alternating bands
scenes.narration: Researchers found repeating light and dark bands along the tail and suggest they may preserve evidence of camouflage or body patterning.

scenes.title: Other soft structures survived too
scenes.narration: The fossil also preserves possible sensory structures and soft-tissue features related to breathing.

scenes.title: It may be among the oldest crocodylomorph color patterns
scenes.narration: If the interpretation is correct, this could be among the oldest known body patterns in a crocodylomorph, though the original pigment colors themselves are not preserved.

scenes.title: Different light can reveal a different fossil
scenes.narration: A fossil that looks like plain rock in visible light can still hold hidden clues about skin, anatomy, and life more than a hundred million years ago.
